correctness.rationale: Normalized Box cube maps depend exactly on the primal two-section adjacency. In degree one, 2-cube boundaries impose reversals, 3-cycle, and 4-cycle relations. Hyperedge-witness transfer of closed walks descends modulo these relations, and the transposed construction is its inverse up to fillings of triangles within hyperedges. The proof is integral and handles disconnected incidence components. Six small examples were independently computed using signed 2-cube boundaries and integral Smith normal form.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary paper conjectures dual hypergraph homotopy equivalence but does not prove it or the unconditional Box H1 isomorphism. Earlier graph cubical and Dowker nerve results do not directly identify all triangle-and-square relations across the two incidence expansions. Targeted literature and published mathematical-record comparisons found no covering statement; unindexed equivalent formulations remain possible.
residual_risks: A prior paper phrased as low-dimensional incidence homotopy or square-graph path homology could imply the theorem without its present terminology.
Higher-degree duality and hypergraph homotopy equivalence are not established.
Conclusions exclude empty edge sets, empty hyperedges, and unsupported vertices.

value.rationale: The new hypergraph homotopy conjecture makes dual-invariant Box homology a necessary test. The theorem gives its complete integral degree-one answer for every supported finite hypergraph by a transparent inverse cycle map, eliminating all such first-degree obstructions at once and identifying higher degrees as the only possible Box-homology obstruction. It is a structural unrestricted theorem, not a numerical sample or a trivial parameter substitution.
